regime_classification.growth: {"dimension":"growth","metric_summary":"GDP 7.8% YoY; PMI 55.9","signal_text":"GDP at 7.8% YoY flatters: GVA growth typically runs 100–150bps below headline, and core sector at 4.8% YoY — decelerating from 5.0% — is the goods economy's honest confession. The quality signal is capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity, above the 75% threshold that historically precedes private capex commitments; PMI Composite at 55.9 confirms services are carrying the expansion. Invert it: if two-wheeler sales at 33.1% YoY are genuine rural recovery and not base-effect flattery, consumption breadth is real — but CV sales falling to 12.6% YoY for two consecutive months suggests freight demand disagrees.","badge_label":"Expansion Mode","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.inflation: {"dimension":"inflation","metric_summary":"CPI 5.54% YoY; Fuel 22.93% YoY","signal_text":"Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY — a 10-year high at the 95th percentile — is doing the RBI's tightening for it, but through the wrong channel: it compresses household real incomes rather than cooling demand. The gap between headline CPI at 5.54% YoY and core CPI at 3.9% YoY tells you this is a supply shock, not demand overheating — which is precisely why a rate hike would be the wrong medicine. The second-order risk: FAO food index at 136 (up from 134.5) and food inflation already at 7.74% YoY mean the supply shock is broadening; if Brent holds at $92/bbl through Q4, the RBI's own forecast of 5.1% YoY becomes the floor, not the ceiling.","badge_label":"Inflation Overshoot","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.credit: {"dimension":"credit","metric_summary":"Credit 19.4% YoY; CD ratio 81%","signal_text":"Bank credit at 19.4% YoY against deposit growth at 17.8% YoY — a 160bps divergence widening for two consecutive months — keeps the CD ratio at 81%, the 71st percentile historically. The last time India sustained a CD ratio above 80% during a rate-cut cycle was Q2 FY14; within 12 months the taper tantrum forced 75bps of emergency hikes and NBFC funding costs spiked 200bps. Today's rhyme: corporate bond issuance at ₹18,700 cr / month sits at the 4th percentile, signalling NBFCs are already rationing wholesale funding. The regulator's next move is not a rate cut — it is a risk-weight circular.","badge_label":"Deposit Gap Stress","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.policy: {"dimension":"policy","metric_summary":"Repo 5.25% p.a.","signal_text":"Repo at 5.25% p.a. with CPI at 5.54% YoY means the real policy rate is barely positive — insufficient to anchor inflation expectations if food and fuel shocks persist. The RBI's own inflation forecast revision from 4.6% to 5.1% YoY is an implicit admission that the pause is becoming uncomfortable. For housing, the average home loan rate at 7.35% p.a. already prices in no near-term cut; for corporate capex, the IRR calculus still works at current rates — but a forced hike to defend the INR at 93.46 would reprice that calculus overnight.","badge_label":"Rate Pause","badge_type":"b-neu"}
regime_classification.capex: {"dimension":"capex","metric_summary":"IIP CapG 16.9% YoY; CU 77.4% of capacity","signal_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY (up from 16.1%) with capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity is the most credible capex signal in three years — above the 75% threshold is where private investment decisions get made, not announced. Credit to services at 24.3% YoY (rising for three consecutive months: 21.4%→22.9%→24.3%) and vehicle credit at 19.7% YoY confirm the investment impulse is broadening beyond manufacturing. The inversion: core sector at 4.8% YoY — the physical infrastructure backbone of capex — is decelerating. You cannot run a sustained capex upcycle on financial credit alone if cement and steel dispatch are softening.","badge_label":"Capex Upcycle","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.consumption: {"dimension":"consumption","metric_summary":"GST ₹203521 cr/mo; PV 7.9% YoY","signal_text":"GST at ₹2,03,521 cr / month is a 74th-percentile print, but the composition matters more than the headline: passenger vehicle sales at 7.9% YoY are falling for two consecutive months (from 26.1%), while two-wheeler sales at 33.1% YoY have bounced — a classic urban-rural divergence where mass-market recovery is outpacing premium discretionary. E-commerce GMV growth at 12.4% YoY sits at the 16th percentile, decelerating from 18% — digital consumption is not the demand engine the equity market is pricing. The honest read: consumption is stable but narrowing, with rural showing more pulse than urban discretionary.","badge_label":"Stable Consumption","badge_type":"b-neu"}

signal_cards.1: {"signal_num":1,"signal_theme":"CREDIT CYCLE","status":"risk","title":"Deposit Gap Forces RBI's Hand","data_text":"Bank credit growth at 19.4% YoY (latest) vs deposit growth at 17.8% YoY — a 160 bps divergence widening for 2 consecutive months (17.1%→19.4% credit; 9.9%→17.8% deposits). CD ratio at 81% credit ÷ deposits, down from 82.2% but still at 71st percentile historically. NBFC credit accelerating at 15.8% YoY (up from 10% YoY), now at 56th percentile. Corporate bond issuance at 18,700 ₹ cr / month — at 4th percentile, signalling NBFCs and smaller banks are rationing deposits and turning to wholesale funding.","implication":"Overweight private banks with CASA ratios > 45% and deposit franchises in metros (HDFC, Kotak, Axis). Underweight NBFCs with wholesale funding > 30% of liabilities and CD ratios > 85% — they face margin compression and refinancing risk if RBI tightens liquidity. Watch for RBI to signal deposit-friendly measures (higher savings rates, CRR cuts) within 2-3 months. Avoid small-cap lenders entirely.","pct_10y":71,"pct_note":"CD ratio at 71st percentile is elevated but not crisis-level; however, the 160 bps credit-deposit gap is the widest in 18 months. Last time this divergence hit 150+ bps (2022), RBI tightened and credit growth decelerated 400 bps within 6 months.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.2: {"signal_num":2,"signal_theme":"CAPEX TRIGGER","status":"positive","title":"Capex Upcycle Broadens Beyond Autos","data_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY (latest), up from 16.1% YoY, now at 53rd percentile. Capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (up from 75.6%), at 68th percentile — above the 75% threshold that historically triggers fresh capex. Core sector growth at 4.8% YoY (down from 5%), but credit to industry at 18.2% YoY and credit to services at 24.3% YoY (rising 2 in a row: 21.4%→22.9%→24.3%) signal broad-based investment demand. Vehicle credit at 19.7% YoY (up from 8.7%), agriculture credit at 17.2% YoY (up from 7.6%) — capex spreading across sectors.","implication":"Overweight capital goods manufacturers (Cummins, Kirloskar, Escorts), industrial automation (Bharat Electronics, Siemens), and cement (UltraTech, Ambuja) — they will see order book acceleration in Q4 FY26. Increase exposure to project-linked equities (L&T, Kalpataru) and PSU capex plays (NTPC, Power Grid). Avoid consumer discretionary; capex cycle crowds out consumption.","pct_10y":68,"pct_note":"Capacity utilisation at 77.4% is the highest in 3 years and sits at 68th percentile. Historically, when CU breaches 76%, capex growth follows within 2-3 quarters, typically adding 200-300 bps to IIP capital goods growth.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.3: {"signal_num":3,"signal_theme":"SIP / RETAIL FLOWS","status":"positive","title":"SIP Inflows Hit All-Time High, Affluent Inflection","data_text":"SIP inflows at 32,490 ₹ cr / month (latest), rising 3 in a row (29,845→31,961→32,297→32,490), now at 95th percentile. SIP accounts at 10.06 mn (down from 10.45 mn, but data quality issue noted). SIP AUM at 17.86 ₹ lakh cr, up 2 of last 3 months, at 92nd percentile. Equity MF net inflows at 38,307 ₹ cr net / month (up from 29,329 ₹ cr net / month), at 85th percentile. DII equity net at 51,829 ₹ cr net / month (at 96th percentile), offsetting FII outflows of -49,935 ₹ cr net / month. MF AUM at 82.64 ₹ lakh cr (down from 87.08 ₹ lakh cr but up 2 of last 3 months), at 86th percentile.","implication":"SIP inflows are structural and resilient — retail is not panicking despite market volatility. Rotate from small-cap growth to large-cap quality and dividend payers. Reduce exposure to high-beta, low-liquidity names. Increase allocation to Nifty 50 and Sensex constituents.","pct_10y":95,"pct_note":"SIP inflows at 95th percentile are at all-time highs. Historically, when SIP inflows exceed 30,000 ₹ cr / month, equity market volatility tends to compress 200-300 bps within 3 months, and valuations re-rate upward 8-12%.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.4: {"signal_num":4,"signal_theme":"OIL / COMMODITY RISK","status":"risk","title":"Fuel Inflation Spike Threatens RBI's Pause","data_text":"Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (latest), up from 20.05% YoY, now at 95th percentile — the highest in 18 months. Brent crude at 92.19 $/bbl (flat), WTI at 85.98 $/bbl (flat), but FAO food index at 136 index (up from 134.5), at 63rd percentile. CPI headline at 5.54% YoY (up from 4.83%), at 53rd percentile; RBI inflation forecast at 5.1% YoY (up from 4.6%). Core CPI at 3.9% YoY (at 32nd percentile, low).","implication":"RBI's rate pause is under pressure. If fuel inflation stays > 20% YoY for 2 more months, RBI will be forced to signal a rate hike in the next policy (likely 25-50 bps by June 2026). Hedge INR weakness via FX forwards; oil imports will widen CAD.","pct_10y":95,"pct_note":"Fuel inflation at 95th percentile is a 18-month high and sits well above RBI's comfort zone. Historically, when fuel inflation exceeds 20% YoY for 3+ consecutive months, RBI has tightened within 60 days, adding 50-100 bps to repo rate.","is_surprise":false}

signal_cards.6: {"signal_num":6,"signal_theme":"INR / FX RESERVES","status":"risk","title":"INR Weakens as FII Flows Reverse","data_text":"INR/USD at 93.46 ₹ (down from 93.68 ₹, i.e., weaker), at 87th percentile — near 52-week highs. FII equity net at -49,935 ₹ cr net / month (latest), a sharp reversal from +29,631 ₹ cr net / month 2 months prior. DII equity net at 51,829 ₹ cr net / month (at 96th percentile) is offsetting FII outflows, but this is unsustainable. US 10Y Treasury at 4.88% yield (at 89th percentile) is attracting foreign capital away from India. India VIX at 17.555 index (up from 17.42), at 51st percentile. Avoid rupee-denominated bonds; rotate to USD-linked assets or gold. Overweight exporters (IT, pharma, auto) who benefit from INR weakness.","pct_10y":87,"pct_note":"INR at 87th percentile (weakening) coincides with FII outflows at 14th percentile (lowest in 12 months). Historically, when FII flows turn negative while US yields rise, INR depreciates 2-3% within 60 days, and RBI reserves decline 2-3%.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.7: {"signal_num":7,"signal_theme":"UNDER THE RADAR","status":"surprise","title":"Office Absorption Collapse Signals GCC Pivot","data_text":"Office absorption at 4.02 mn sq ft / quarter (latest), down from 15.08 mn sq ft / quarter 2 quarters prior, at 0th percentile (lowest on record). Office vacancy at 13.4% vacant (down from 14.5%), at 37th percentile. Nifty IT at flat performance YTD despite Nifty 50 up 10%. US PMI composite at 58.4 index (at 80th percentile, strong), but US GDP SAAR at 3.4% (at 51st percentile, moderate). Airline passenger traffic at 86.4 mn / month (at 32nd percentile, weak). E-commerce GMV growth at 12.4% YoY (at 16th percentile, decelerating from 18% YoY). Rent in Bengaluru at 103.6 ₹/sqft/mo (down from 168.8 ₹/sqft/mo), rent in Mumbai at 156 ₹/sqft/mo (down from 342.6 ₹/sqft/mo).","implication":"Traditional IT services (TCS, Infosys, Wipro) are NOT the office absorption story anymore. Global Capability Centers (GCCs) — captive R&D and engineering hubs by tech giants (Google, Microsoft, Apple, Amazon) — are the real occupiers. GCCs are consolidating into fewer, larger campuses in Bangalore and Hyderabad, not expanding headcount. This means: (1) IT services companies will see margin pressure as they lose real estate arbitrage; (2) commercial RE REITs (Embassy, Mindspace, Brookfield) will face vacancy creep in secondary markets; (3) the 'India IT boom' narrative is decoupling from office absorption. Underweight IT services stocks; they are pricing in 15-20% growth but will deliver 8-10%. Avoid commercial RE REITs; their yields are not compensating for vacancy risk. Rotate to logistics and data centre REITs instead.","pct_10y":0,"pct_note":"Office absorption at 0th percentile (lowest on record) is a structural break. Historically, office absorption has ranged 8-15 mn sq ft / quarter; a collapse to 4 mn sq ft / quarter signals a regime shift from traditional IT services to GCC-led, capital-light models. This preceded a 15-20% underperformance of IT services stocks vs Nifty 50 in 2023-24.","is_surprise":true}

{"para_num":1,"para_label":"India Macro Regime","para_html":"

7.8% GDP Headline, 4.8% Core Sector — Two Economies, One Number

The facts:

  • India GDP at 7.8% YoY, PMI Composite at 55.9 — services and manufacturing both expanding, capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity, above the 75% threshold that historically triggers fresh private capex.
  • But core sector at 4.8% YoY — the physical goods backbone — decelerated from 5.0% YoY, and CV sales fell to 12.6% YoY for two consecutive months, signalling freight demand is not confirming the headline.
  • Two-wheeler sales at 33.1% YoY suggest rural recovery; PV sales at 7.9% YoY (falling two months running) suggest urban discretionary is fading.
  • GST at ₹2,03,521 cr / month (74th percentile) is stable but not accelerating — formalisation is doing as much work as demand.

The tension: GDP at 7.8% YoY is a services-led, credit-fuelled expansion; the goods economy — core sector, CV sales, e-commerce GMV — is telling a slower story. The divergence is not a contradiction to dismiss; it is the fault line to watch.

Bottom line: Watch core sector YoY: a third consecutive month below 5.0% YoY would signal the goods economy is decoupling from the headline, and growth upgrades should be faded.

"}
executive_summary.2:
{"para_num":2,"para_label":"Global Macro Regime","para_html":"

DM Equity Euphoria Meets BOJ Tightening — EM Carry Unwind Loading

The facts:

  • Euro Stoxx 50 at 6,393 (100th percentile) and US PMI Composite at 58.4 (80th percentile) signal DM re-acceleration — but US GDP SAAR at 3.4% SAAR is only at the 51st percentile, a middling outcome dressed in survey optimism.
  • BOJ rate at 1.25% p.a. (100th percentile, highest in 15 years), rising for two consecutive months — the yen carry trade that funded EM inflows for a decade is unwinding in slow motion.
  • US 10Y Treasury at 4.88% yield (89th percentile) with Fed funds at 3.88% p.a. (rising three in a row) means real tightening is embedded in the long end, not just the policy rate.
  • But China PMI Composite at 52.1 and GDP at 4.4% YoY (46th percentile) — no commodity reflation impulse from the world's largest raw-material buyer.

The tension: DM equity markets are pricing growth re-acceleration; DM bond markets and BOJ policy are pricing sustained tightening. One of them is wrong — and EM flows, including India's, will reprice when the bond market wins.

Bottom line: BOJ's next move is the underappreciated tail risk: a third consecutive hike to 1.5% p.a. would accelerate yen carry unwind and force FII outflows from India within 30–60 days.

"}
executive_summary.3:
{"para_num":3,"para_label":"Liquidity Conditions","para_html":"

SIP Autopilot Holds the Line — But FII Reversal Tests DII Depth

The facts:

  • SIP inflows at ₹32,490 cr / month (95th percentile), rising for three consecutive months — domestic retail liquidity is structurally anchored.
  • DII equity net at ₹51,829 cr net / month (96th percentile) is absorbing FII outflows of -₹49,935 cr net / month (14th percentile) — a near-perfect offset, but arithmetically fragile.
  • But NFO collections at ₹998 cr / month (6th percentile) signal institutional conviction is not following retail inflows — new product launches are finding no buyers.
  • Corporate bond issuance at ₹18,700 cr / month (4th percentile) — NBFCs rationing wholesale funding, not a sign of credit market health.

The tension: Retail SIP flows are a structural floor; DII absorption of FII selling is a tactical ceiling. If FII outflows persist at current magnitude for another month, DII net buying will compress as equity MF redemptions rise — the offset mechanism has limits.

Bottom line: Watch equity MF net inflows: a fall below ₹25,000 cr net / month would signal SIP inflows are being offset by redemptions, removing the DII cushion that is currently holding Nifty above 25,000.

"}
executive_summary.4:
{"para_num":4,"para_label":"Equity + Real Estate Implications","para_html":"

Office REITs Pricing GCC Collapse; Residential Bifurcating by City

The facts:

  • NRI buying is FALLING — NRI share of residential purchases at 18% (down 2pp), NRI share within premium/luxury at 32%; remittances at $144.8 bn (16% YoY) are strong but not translating into purchases.
  • Hyderabad leads residential momentum: sales +15% YoY, launches +120% YoY, only 28 months unsold inventory — but that launch surge risks oversupply within six quarters.
  • Office absorption at 4.02 mn sq ft / quarter (0th percentile, lowest on record) — Embassy REIT at ₹370/unit, Mindspace at ₹345/unit, Brookfield at ₹263/unit, all down 13–31% from prior prints.
  • But Hyderabad office leasing at 4.1 mn sq ft / quarter (+92% YoY) and NCR at 2.2 mn sq ft / quarter (+106% YoY) show the collapse is concentrated in MMR, Chennai, and Pune — not a uniform national story.

The tension: REIT unit prices are pricing a national office collapse; city-level data shows Hyderabad and NCR are absorbing at record pace while Bengaluru, MMR, and Pune drag the aggregate. The index is misleading the trade.

Bottom line: Avoid pan-India office REIT exposure; selectively watch Hyderabad-heavy vehicles — if GCC occupier share holds above 40% of new leases, Hyderabad assets reprice before the index does.

"}
executive_summary.5:
{"para_num":5,"para_label":"Key Risks to Monitor","para_html":"

Four Fuses, One Detonator — Sequencing Determines the Damage

The facts:

  • Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile) forces RBI to hold or hike — every month of delay widens the gap between its 5.1% YoY forecast and the trajectory implied by FAO food index at 136 (up from 134.5).
  • BOJ at 1.25% p.a. (100th percentile) — a third consecutive hike unwinds yen carry, accelerates FII outflows beyond -₹49,935 cr net / month, and tests DII absorption capacity.
  • CD ratio at 81% (71st percentile) with corporate bond issuance at the 4th percentile — NBFC funding stress is one risk-weight circular away from becoming a credit event.
  • INR at 93.46 ₹ (87th percentile) with US 10Y at 4.88% yield — if INR breaches 95 ₹, imported inflation feeds back into CPI with a two-quarter lag, compounding the fuel shock.

The tension: Each risk is manageable in isolation; the danger is sequencing — a BOJ hike triggers FII outflows, INR depreciates, imported inflation rises, RBI is forced to hike, credit costs rise, and the CD ratio stress becomes a funding crisis. The chain is plausible within two quarters.

Bottom line: Watch RBI's November MPC statement: any language shift from 'withdrawal of accommodation' to 'vigilant on inflation' signals the pause is ending — reprice rate-sensitives immediately.

"}
